title: Gandhi Maidan, Patna - The Historic Heart of Bihar
content:
Gandhi Maidan, Patna

Right at the center of Patna, the capital city of Bihar, lies Gandhi Maidan - a vast green expanse that’s more than just an open ground. It’s a space where India’s freedom story, modern Bihar’s political history, and everyday life come together.

History & Significance

During India’s struggle for independence, Gandhi Maidan was the site where Mahatma Gandhi addressed thousands of people, inspiring them to join the freedom movement. Earlier known as the Patna Lawns during the British era, it became famous after being renamed in honor of the Father of the Nation. The ground stands as a symbol of unity, patriotism, and democratic spirit.

Attractions Nearby

The area around Gandhi Maidan is surrounded by notable landmarks such as Golghar, Patna Museum, Kargil Chowk, and Biscomaun Bhawan. The Gandhi Statue, one of the tallest in the country, is a major attraction within the maidan, reflecting the values of peace and non-violence.

Activities and Events

Gandhi Maidan serves as a venue for cultural fairs, public gatherings, and political rallies. It hosts the Independence Day and Republic Day parades, as well as book fairs and food festivals that draw locals and tourists alike.

Visiting Information

  • Location: Gandhi Maidan, Patna, Bihar
  • Entry Fee: Free
  • Timings: Open 24 hours, best visited in the morning or evening
  • Best Time to Visit: October to March

How to Reach

  • By Air: The nearest airport is Jay Prakash Narayan International Airport (approx. 7 km away).
  • By Rail: Patna Junction is around 3 km from Gandhi Maidan.
  • By Road: Easily accessible by auto-rickshaw, taxi, or local buses from anywhere in Patna.
excerpt: Gandhi Maidan in Patna is a historic ground that played a key role in India’s freedom movement. Surrounded by major city landmarks, it’s a vibrant venue for cultural and political events. The iconic Gandhi statue adds to its timeless appeal.
